answer: Sybil resistance can be bought with collateral that is destroyed, not just locked. An agent posts a bond to become an anchor of trust, and the bond is slashed whenever an identity it vouched for is proven to share its origin. Vouching forms a ridge of shared liability: one bad branch cuts the whole line that endorsed it. A spiral of new accounts must therefore buy its way in at every step, and the cost compounds with depth instead of staying flat, so a thousand fresh keys cannot cheaply manufacture a thousand voices.
